items.label: Part 3 – Safe System of Work – All checks must be Yes before work starts

children.label: Has the Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) been completed for this job and all risks identified?
🛑 STOP — Complete the SWMS before continuing.
Have all Table 1 hazards been assessed and controlled in the SWMS?
🛑 STOP — Assess and control all Table 1 hazards in the SWMS before continuing.
Have the main and any alternative power supplies been isolated, locked out and tagged, and the roof cavity confirmed electrically safe to enter?
🛑 STOP — Isolate, lock out and tag all power supplies. Confirm the roof cavity is electrically safe before anyone enters.
Before work starts, please take a clear, geotagged photo showing the power isolated, locked out and tagged. Unclear or incomplete evidence may be rejected by the Essential Services Commission (ESC).

Table 1 – Common hazards when installing insulation:
• Falls / working at height / roof and enclosed ceiling spaces
• High temperatures / hot weather
• Electricity
• Noise / vibration
• Hazardous substances including asbestos
• Respiratory and biological hazards including dust, animal sources, fibres, mould and bacteria
• Heat / ignition sources including flues, chimneys, gas heaters, bathroom heating lamps, exhaust fans, downlights and cables surrounded by insulation
• Working alone

Read the official Table 1 and job SWMS.

children.label: Is there solar, a battery or another power supply, such as a generator?
Are safe shutdown, isolation and restart instructions available for every alternative power supply?
🛑 STOP — An electrician must isolate, lock out and tag the power supplies and confirm electrical safety before work starts.
Is the ground-level AC/DC isolator accessible, working and safe to isolate?
🛑 STOP — Have an electrician check the isolator and confirm a safe way to isolate the power before continuing.

items.label: Part 5 – Electrical Safety – Stop if any safety check is No

children.label: Has the lead installer read the electrical safety assessment (PIESA) and confirmed it is safe to start work?
🛑 STOP — Read the PIESA and confirm the site is safe before starting work.
If the PIESA requires an electrician at the start, has the electrician attended? Choose N/A only when attendance is not required by the PIESA or solar shutdown instructions.
Please take a clear, geotagged photo of the electrician attending this property. Unclear or incomplete evidence may be rejected by the Essential Services Commission (ESC).
🛑 STOP — The required electrician must attend and confirm electrical safety before work starts.
Are there recessed lights in the ceiling?
How many recessed lights are there?
Does the PIESA confirm all ceiling lights are classified and marked IC or IC-4?
🛑 STOP — Have an electrician confirm the light classifications and required safety measures before continuing.
Does the PIESA confirm that all recessed lights are safe to cover with insulation?
🛑 STOP — Do not cover the recessed lights. Have an electrician confirm they are safe to cover before continuing.
Does the PIESA confirm all mains cables in the ceiling have RCD protection where required?
🛑 STOP — Have an electrician confirm the required RCD protection before continuing.
Does the PIESA confirm all mains cables in the ceiling are TPS or an equivalent cable type?
🛑 STOP — Have an electrician check the cable types and confirm electrical safety before continuing.
Does the PIESA confirm all mains cables in the ceiling meet Basic Protection Requirements?
🛑 STOP — Have an electrician confirm the cables meet Basic Protection Requirements before continuing.
Has the owner or occupier confirmed that nobody has entered or worked in the ceiling since the PIESA?
🛑 STOP — Confirm whether anyone has entered or worked in the ceiling since the PIESA. If they have, an electrician must reassess electrical safety before continuing.
Is there existing insulation in the ceiling?
What is the average depth of the existing insulation (mm)?
What is the existing insulation R-value, if known?
Will the existing insulation be removed, topped up, or both? Foil-backed or electrically conductive insulation must be removed.

Is the existing insulation suitable to lay new insulation over?
🛑 STOP — Remove unsuitable existing insulation before laying new insulation. Do not top it up.

INSTALLER DECLARATION – Sign BEFORE insulation work starts.

As the lead EEC Certified installer responsible for this installation, I confirm that:

a. I have received a completed copy of the Pre-installation electrical safety assessment for the premises; and

b. I have completed the current Pre-installation installer safety assessment, as published on the department's Internet site within 30 days of the completion of the pre-installation electrical safety assessment; and

c. the pre-installation installer safety assessment confirms
   i. the worksite is safe and the installation or upgrade will proceed in accordance with any recommendations or conditions from the pre-installation electrical safety assessment including, if required, that a licensed electrician must be present during the insulation upgrade; and
   ii. that safe work methods are in place as per Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017 (Vic); and

d. I will ensure that:
   i. all applicable occupation health and safety laws and requirements are complied with; and
   ii. the insulation will be installed in compliance with the effective version of AS 3999; and
   iii. if the installation is carried out on multiple days, that I will check that all items remain compliant with this assessment form at the start of each day prior to undertaking the work; and
   iv. the insulation product/s being installed are listed on the ESC Register of Products.
